title.rendered: Enter His Gates with Thanksgiving: The Doorway into His Presence | The Thankful Heart, Day 1

excerpt.rendered: Psalm 100:4 shows the way into God’s presence: through the gates with thanksgiving. Day 1 of The Thankful Heart begins fourteen days of gratitude leading into Advent.

content.rendered:
Thanksgiving is not the reward at the end of a good week. It is the gate at the start of every day. You do not give thanks to get in; you give thanks because the gate is already open.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, November 15, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 1

Today’s Scripture

“Enter into His gates with thanksgiving, and into His courts with praise. Be thankful to Him, and bless His name. For the Lord is good; His mercy is everlasting, and His truth endures to all generations.”
Psalm 100:4-5 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

For the last fourteen days we learned to live from rest. Now, for the next fourteen, leading us right up to the first Sunday of Advent, we learn to live from thanks. The two belong together. A heart that has found its rest in Christ starts to overflow, and the overflow sounds like gratitude.

Psalm 100 is a song for pilgrims arriving at the temple. They have walked for days. They are dusty and tired. And as the gates come into view, the psalm tells them how to go in: with thanksgiving. Not with complaints about the road. Not with a list of requests. With thanks. Thanksgiving was the doorway, and praise filled the courts beyond it.

Notice the reason the psalm gives. “For the Lord is good; His mercy is everlasting.” We do not give thanks because everything around us is good. We give thanks because He is good, and His mercy does not run out. Circumstances change by the hour. His goodness does not. That is why thanksgiving can be the first word of the day, even on a hard day.

Under the new covenant, the gates are not in Jerusalem. Hebrews 10 tells us we now have boldness to enter the Holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way. The way in has been opened at the cross. So when we come with thanksgiving, we are not earning entry. We are responding to an open door. Gratitude is simply the right posture of someone who knows they have been welcomed home.

Here is a simple practice for these fourteen days. Before you ask God for anything, thank Him for three things He has already done. Name them out loud. His presence that has never left you. His grace that covered yesterday. His goodness in something small you almost missed. Start at the gate. The courts are not far behind.

How the Thankful Heart Enters

It starts with thanks, not requests. Thanksgiving is the gate; praise is the courtyard.

It rests on who He is. The Lord is good, and His mercy is everlasting, whatever the day holds.

It walks through an open door. Christ has opened the way; gratitude is our response, not our payment.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You that the way into Your presence is already open through the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 10:19-20). I enter Your gates with thanksgiving and Your courts with praise. I thank You that You are good, that Your mercy is everlasting, and that Your truth endures to all generations (Psalm 100:5). Today I begin with thanks: for Your presence that never leaves me, for Your grace that covered yesterday, and for Your goodness in the small things. My heart is thankful because You are faithful. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
